notes:
======
{
  const get_distinct_channels_in_slot = (slot) => {
    const obj = {}
    for (let program of slot) {
      obj[ program.channel ] = true
    }
    return Object.keys(obj).sort()
  }

  for (let slot_name of Object.keys(data.slots)) {
    const channels = get_distinct_channels_in_slot(data.slots[slot_name])

    console.log('slot "' + slot_name + '" has ' + channels.length + ' channels:', channels.join(', '))
  }
}

output:
=======
slot "now"   has 5 channels: 4S, C4, E4, F4, M4
slot "next"  has 5 channels: 4S, C4, E4, F4, M4
slot "later" has 5 channels: 4S, C4, E4, F4, M4

notes (request):
================
* the unique id for each channel (ex: "C4") is included in the DOM data

notes (response):
=================
* the data structure for livetv streams is nearly identical to VOD streams
  - VOD:
      data.subtitlesAssets = [{format, url}]
      data.videoProfiles = [{name, streams: [{uri, token}]}]
      ----
      data.subtitlesAssets.map(obj => obj.format).join(', ') === "webvtt_007, srt_009, webvtt_003"
        where: "webvtt_003" is an .m3u8
      data.videoProfiles.map(obj => obj.name).join(', ') === "dashpr-dyn-stream-1, dashwv-dyn-stream-1, hls-dyn-stream-1"
        where: PLAY_READY, WIDEVINE, FAIR_PLAY
  - live:
      data.channelInfo.videoProfiles = [{name, streams: [{uri, token}]}]
      ----
      data.channelInfo.videoProfiles.map(obj => obj.name).join(', ') === "dashpr-live-stream-iso-dash-sp-tl, dashpr-dai-live-stream-iso-dash-mp-tl, dashwv-live-stream-iso-dash-sp-tl, dashwv-dai-live-stream-iso-dash-mp-tl, fps-livestream-1, fps-livestream-yospace-1"
* all WIDEVINE streams have a name that begins with: 'dashwv-'

question:
=========
assuming that Widevine license acquisition for livetv channel streams follows the same procedure as VOD,
then what is the "request_id" parameter value sent in the request?
  - VOD uses the "assetId" for the episode
  - live channels don't appear to have any "assetId"
